source: the RNA polymerase error rate is >4 orders of magnitude higher than that of DNA polymerase
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data or citation in this manuscript.

claim: Transcription errors are amplified more than 1000-fold due to translation.
source: errors are amplified >1000-fold due to translation
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data or citation in this manuscript.

claim: Current methods to measure RNA polymerase fidelity are low-throughput.
source: current methods to measure RNA polymerase fidelity are low-throughout, technically challenging, and organism specific
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge without specific citation or data.

claim: Current methods to measure RNA polymerase fidelity are technically challenging.
source: current methods to measure RNA polymerase fidelity are low-throughout, technically challenging, and organism specific

claim: Changes in RNA polymerase fidelity can be measured using standard RNA sequencing protocols.
source: Here I show that changes in RNA polymerase fidelity can be measured using standard RNA sequencing protocols.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by the methods and experimental approach described in the manuscript.

claim: RNA polymerase is error-prone.
source: I find that RNA polymerase is error-prone
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study, supported by the experimental measurements described in the methods.

claim: RNA polymerase errors can result in splicing defects.
source: I find that RNA polymerase is error-prone, and these errors can result in splicing defects.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study, supported by the measurement of error rates at splice junctions described in the methods.

claim: Differential expression of RNA polymerase subunits causes changes in RNA polymerase fidelity.
source: I find that differential expression of RNA polymerase subunits causes changes in RNA polymerase fidelity
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study, supported by the experimental manipulation of RPB9 and DST1 expression levels described in the methods.

claim: Coding sequences may have evolved to minimize the effect of RNA polymerase errors.
source: I find that differential expression of RNA polymerase subunits causes changes in RNA polymerase fidelity, and that coding sequences may have evolved to minimize the effect of these errors.
evidence: This is stated as a finding with speculative language ('may have'), suggesting inference from the data rather than direct experimental demonstration.

claim: Errors caused by RNA polymerase may be a major source of stochastic variability at the level of single cells.
source: These results suggest that errors caused by RNA polymerase may be a major source of stochastic variability at the level of single cells.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative conclusion ('suggest', 'may be') inferred from the findings of the study.

claim: Alignment is the most computationally expensive step of the RNA-seq analysis pipeline.
source: In order to bypass alignment, which is the most computationally expensive step of the pipeline
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the methods section without specific citation.

claim: Increased mismatch rates occur at splice junctions due to alignment problems with both spliced and unspliced reads.
source: in order to avoid increased mismatch rates at splice junctions due to alignment problems with both spliced and unspliced reads
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge that motivated the methodological approach.

claim: SAMtools can be used to remove alignments that do not align along the full length of the genome.
source: I used SAMtools (Li et al., 2009) and awk to remove all alignments that do not align along the full length of the genome
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation to the SAMtools publication.

claim: For 76 bp reads, only reads with a CIGAR flag of 76 M represent full-length alignments.
source: for 76 bp reads, only reads with a CIGAR flag of 76 M
evidence: This is stated as technical knowledge about sequence alignment formats.

claim: The first and last 10 bp of each read were trimmed and converted to Ns with quality strings set to '!'.
source: The remaining reads weretrimmed (bamUtil, trimBam) to convert the first and last 10 bp of each read to Ns and set the quality strings to '!'.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the data processing steps performed.

claim: Positions with more than one read of the same nonreference base were not counted in the error analysis.
source: Positions with too many errors (e.g., more than one read of the same nonreference base) were not counted.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the filtering criteria used in the analysis.

claim: The UCSC table browser can be used to download bed files for genomic features.
source: I used the University of California Santa Cruz (UCSC) table browser (Karolchik, 2004) to download two bed files
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation to the UCSC table browser publication.

claim: Bedtools can be used to generate bed files with intervals containing splicing donor and acceptor sites.
source: I then used bedtools (Quinlan and Hall, 2010) (bedtools flank -b 20 -l 0 and bedtools flank -l 20 -b 0) to generate bed files with intervals that contain the splicing donor and acceptor sites, respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation to the bedtools publication.

claim: Only introns flanked by GT and AG donor and acceptor sites were kept in the analysis.
source: I used bedtools getfasta on the +10 bp flanking bed file to keep only introns flanked by GT and AG donor and acceptor sites.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the filtering criteria used in the analysis.

claim: The error rate at each position is calculated as the sum of all errors at that position divided by the sum of all reads.
source: The error rate at each position (e.g., -10, -9, -8, etc. from the G at the 5' donor site) is the sum of all errors at that position, divided by the sum of all reads.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the calculation performed.

claim: Positions are relative to the splicing feature, not to the genome, because error rates at any single genomic position are dominated by sampling bias.
source: Positions are relative to the splicing feature, not to the genome, as error rates at any single genomic position are dominated by sampling bias.
evidence: This is a methodological statement with reasoning based on knowledge of sampling bias.
